sections.h2: Is there a transfer tax in Wheeling?
sections.html:
Not from the village. Wheeling has no real estate transfer tax of its own. It does require every seller to obtain a Real Estate Transfer Stamp on the original deed, and the stamp carries no fee. The catch is that the stamp is only issued after the final water, sewer and garbage charges, plus any outstanding tickets and penalties, are paid in full.

The state tax still applies. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, Illinois taxes the privilege of transferring title at 50 cents per $500 of value stated in the declaration, and the county where the parcel sits can add its own.

sections.h2: How the Wheeling transfer stamp works
sections.html:
The rule sits in Section 15.10 of the Wheeling Municipal Code. The seller presents the original deed at the Finance Department counter in Village Hall, or mails it in, and the stamp is placed on that deed. The village asks for 10 business days of notice before closing so it can schedule a final meter reading and prepare the stamp.

Wheeling transfer stamp requirements
Stamp topicRequirement
Who must obtain a stampAll Wheeling owners, including condominium owners
Other transfers coveredRefinances, quit claim deeds, transfers to a trust
Notice before closing10 business days from the seller
Final water readingDone electronically 2 business days before closing
Fee for the stampNone
ContactWater Billing, (847) 459-2607 or waterbilling@wheelingil.gov

Give the village a forwarding address and the final reading date. Buyers then supply new resident registration information, and if registration is incomplete the village may discontinue water service.

Condo owners pay for water, sewer and garbage through monthly assessments, but the village still treats them as owners who need a stamp. A condo seller therefore has two sets of paperwork: the association's payoff and resale documents, and the village's stamp. Ask the management company early for its timeline, because the association's letter and the village's 10 business day notice both feed the closing date.

  • Order the association paperwork as soon as a contract exists.
  • Submit the village's transfer stamp application at the same time.
  • Keep a copy of the original deed, since the village stamps the original.

Owners occupy 62.7% of Wheeling homes, which leaves a large share of rentals. The typical owner-occupied value is $266,200, rent is $1,663 a month and household income is $85,205, across 15,171 households. Population is estimated at 38,391 for July 2025, 2.0% below the 2020 base.

Monthly owner costs are $1,909 with a mortgage and $892 without. Because so many homes are rented, investors and landlords are an active part of the buyer pool, and a seller with tenants in place should expect questions about lease terms.

Most of Wheeling lies in Cook County, in Wheeling Township, with a smaller part in Lake County. Cook County reassesses one-third of the county each year, and the north suburbs, Wheeling Township included, were reassessed in 2025. Wheeling Township takes in all or part of Wheeling, Arlington Heights, Des Plaines, Glenview, Mount Prospect, Northbrook, Palatine, Prospect Heights, Rolling Meadows and Buffalo Grove, so neighbors across a municipal line share the same assessment cycle. Owners in the Lake County portion should ask the Lake County treasurer and assessor for their schedule.

The Cook County Assessor put the township's median 2024 single-family sale price at $457,000 against a median market value estimate of $429,000. Your closing agent prorates the unpaid tax, so request a copy of the most recent bill before you list.

Many Wheeling houses and condos are rented, and a sale does not end a lease. Tell every prospective buyer what the lease says: the rent, the end date and any deposit you hold. A cash buyer who wants the unit empty should say so before the contract is signed, so you can plan notice to the tenant.

Keep rent and utility records handy. The village stamp depends on the final water, sewer and garbage charges being paid, and a tenant who runs up a balance can delay the stamp. Check the account a few weeks ahead and clear anything outstanding, including tickets and penalties.

Closing is also the moment to hand over keys, garage openers and any warranty papers, and to pass the buyer the tenant's contact details and the lease itself.

Wheeling is a village in Cook and Lake counties about 23 miles northwest of downtown Chicago, in Wheeling and Vernon townships. Metra's North Central Service stops in Wheeling on weekdays only, and Pace buses connect to Des Plaines and Buffalo Grove. Public schools are run by Wheeling Community Consolidated School District 21 and Township High School District 214, which operates Wheeling High School.

Winters are usually very cold and snowy and summers are hot and humid, so buyers look closely at roofs, gutters and furnaces when they walk a house. Drainage and basement moisture are on most inspection lists, so fix or disclose them early.

sections.h2: Getting ready for a quick sale
sections.html:
Start with the village paperwork, because it has the longest lead time. Then gather the Illinois disclosure report required for one to four unit homes before a contract is signed under 765 ILCS 77/20, and a recent tax bill. An investor who pays cash and takes the house as-is still needs the stamp, the final water reading and the paid utility balance, so those steps do not shorten with a faster closing.

  • Call Water Billing at (847) 459-2607 about 10 business days before the closing date.
  • Pay any outstanding tickets and penalties with the village.
  • Have the original deed available, since a copy will not be stamped.
  • Have the closing agent confirm the county's recording charges.

sections.h2: What happens at the closing table
sections.html:
You sign the deed, the title company pays off any mortgage from your proceeds, and the stamped original goes to the county for recording. If the final water bill is not paid, the stamp is not issued and the recording waits, so settle it a few days ahead. Ask the title company for a closing statement that lists every charge, and keep it with your tax records.

If the house sits in the Lake County portion of the village, the recording happens at the Lake County Clerk instead of Cook County, so ask the title company which office applies. Either way, the stamp comes first and the recording follows, and a clear paper trail of paid utility bills makes both steps quick.

faqs.q: Does the Village of Wheeling charge a transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. The village has no real estate transfer tax, but it requires a transfer stamp on the original deed. The stamp has no fee, and all water, sewer, garbage charges, tickets and penalties must be paid first.

faqs.q: How much notice does Wheeling need before closing?
faqs.a: The village asks for 10 business days of notice. The electronic final water reading happens 2 business days before closing, so the longer notice gives staff time to prepare the stamp.

faqs.q: Do condo owners in Wheeling need a transfer stamp?
faqs.a: Yes. The requirement applies to condominium owners even though they pay water, sewer and garbage indirectly through monthly assessments. It also covers refinances, quit claim deeds and transfers into a trust.

faqs.q: Which agency assesses a Wheeling house for tax?
faqs.a: The Cook County Assessor handles most of Wheeling, since the village lies mainly in Cook County. Wheeling Township was reassessed in 2025. Owners in the Lake County portion deal with Lake County offices instead.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Wheeling?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $266,200 for 2020 to 2024. The July 2025 population estimate is 38,391, and median gross rent is $1,663.
